name: Frankie Armas
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember drawing my family as three people around one door.” People around the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio know Frankie by a small Sunday habit. Frankie notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I used to think my family was embarrassing. I asked the graduate to teach me that three-person turn.
appearance: Frankie has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for a loose dark braid. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. In conversation Frankie gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Frankie loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Frankie remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To learn a version of the turn for another family.
family: Liv Oren is Frankie’s older cousin. After a relative came home with a walker, everyone offered errands and nobody remembered the threshold. The two of them still measure doors before offering a room to anyone. Frankie notices the humiliation of having to ask. Asked about *Ten fingers*, Liv says, “I kept trying to pose the hands until she grabbed the kettle.”
connections: Elaine Alcázar. The younger child gets to watch a turn another student wants to learn.

reactions.situation: One of the fathers misses the dance rehearsal
reactions.response: Frankie keeps the missed step available for a quiet practice before the ceremony.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Frankie accepts a small agreed amount if paying lets the neighbor keep their pride.
